Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. The New Zealand players are out in the middle. Tanzid Hasan and Saif Hassan to open for Bangladesh. Nathan Smith to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

Advantage, Bangladesh - Bangladesh delivered a brilliant, high-stakes performance to keep the series alive, with a clinical display of bowling. While Taskin Ahmed and Shoriful Islam set an aggressive tone with the new ball, it was Rana’s relentless spell that truly dictated the terms.\ Utilizing a barrage of sharp, uncomfortable short balls, Rana dismantled the New Zealand batting order to claim a decisive five-wicket haul. Although Hossain and Mehidy provided vital support to keep the pressure on, Rana’s five-fer acted as the wrecking ball that broke the backbone of the Kiwi lineup and shifted the momentum firmly in Bangladesh's favor. Now, Bangladesh are clear favourites. The pitch is on the slower side but the home team should get the job done. Stay tuned.

Far from enough by the Kiwis - New Zealand managed to scrape their way toward a 200-run total, though it was far from a vintage performance. At the halfway point, they sat at a sluggish 97/3, struggling to find any real momentum against a disciplined bowling attack. While Kelly anchored the innings with a gritty maiden fifty and attempted to shift gears late in his knock, he found the acceleration difficult to sustain. His departure for a well-made 83 exposed a middle order that failed to capitalize on their starts, remarkably, no other batter managed to cross the 20-run threshold. With Abbas’s 19 ranking as the second-highest score of the innings, the scorecard told a clear story of a side heavily reliant on a single individual to carry them to a competitive mark.

PITCH REPORT -  HD Ackermann is pitchside and he reports that today's pitch features symmetrical side boundaries of 64 and 63 metres, with a longer 79-metre hit straight down the ground and a crosswind to consider. He observes that the surface has more grass than the previous match, which should help hold it together, though he warns that cracks may emerge if moisture isn't maintained. Overall, Ackermann expects this to be a superior batting surface compared to the first ODI.

Bangladesh captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz  - Miraz views this must-win match as a significant opportunity, expressing confidence that his team can secure a victory if they perform to their potential. He describes the wicket as batting-friendly but believes the bowlers can restrict the opposition if they capitalize on chances and secure early wickets in the first ten overs. Miraz adds that he is counting on his bowlers to step up and bowl economically. Mehidy Hasan Miraz informs that they have a change from the previous XI with Afif Hossain being replaced by Soumya Sarkar.

New Zealand captain Tom Latham - Latham says that the surface appears slightly different than the previous match, the dry conditions underneath should offer similar characteristics. Tom adds that the team’s focus remains on playing the match in front of them, acknowledging that while a series win is within reach, much work remains to be done. Tom Latham informs that they are unchanged for this contest.

Kiwi pacer, Blair Tickner - Blair Tickner credits his success in the first ODI to New Zealand’s strategy of mixing up bowling options as the wicket became lower and slower. Blair adds that the team is enjoying the warmth and feels well supported by the staff in their preparation. Tickner reckons that he feels confident following the opening win, believing that their ability to adapt and take games deep is essential for the close contests expected in these conditions.

Bangladesh opener, Saif Hassan - Saif reflects on his first ODI performance, noting that while he started well and he aims to build a larger innings in the future to support his team better. He acknowledges that while the wicket behaved unevenly during the second innings, and says that adapting to such challenging conditions is a core responsibility for international players rather than an excuse. Looking ahead to today's match, Hassan says that the team played well overall but highlights the need to better manage key moments and avoid losing wickets at critical junctures to improve their results.

Spin vs stability - The game is likely to be won or lost in the middle overs, specifically the battle between Bangladesh's spinners and New Zealand's adaptability. Blair Tickner, who triggered the previous collapse with a four-wicket haul, will be the primary threat again for the visitors. On the other side, Bangladesh will rely on Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Rishad Hossain to dry up runs and force errors. If Bangladesh can prevent another mid-innings muck-up and build a solid partnership, they have the bowling firepower to level the series, otherwise, New Zealand's clinical efficiency is poised to seal it. Middle-order frailties - For Bangladesh, the first match was a story of missed opportunities and a costly middle-period slowdown. Despite promising half-centuries from Saif Hassan and Towhid Hridoy, the team suffered a collapse in the death overs. The primary concern for the hosts remains the lack of defining partnerships in the middle overs, where batters like Afif Hossain struggled to rotate the strike effectively. To stay in the series, the top order must provide a more stable foundation, and the middle order must find a way to navigate the spin-squeeze applied by the Kiwis.

Clinical under pressure - New Zealand's performance in the first ODI was a masterclass in seizing critical moments. Despite fielding an understrength side, they maintained composure to defend a target of 248. Key contributions came from Henry Nicholls, who anchored the innings, and Dean Foxcroft, whose late-innings provided much-needed momentum. To improve further, the Kiwis will want their top order, specifically Will Young and Tom Latham, to convert their starts into more substantial totals to avoid over-reliance on the lower middle order.

A chance to bounce back, a chance to finish - Bangladesh and New Zealand return to the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium for the 2nd ODI, with the visitors holding a 1-0 lead. What began as a test between a settled home side and a new-look touring unit has quickly turned into a high-stakes contest, with Bangladesh fighting to stay alive and New Zealand sensing a chance to seal the series early. Bangladesh's promise, now for precision - There was enough in the first ODI to suggest Bangladesh aren't far away. Half-centuries from Saif Hassan and Tawhid Hridoy, along with a start from Litton Das, showed that the batting has the base, but the lack of a defining partnership proved costly. This is a lineup that has more to offer. Najmul Hossain Shanto at the top and the experience of Mehidy Hasan Miraz in the middle remain crucial, while the likes of Tanzid Hasan will look to build on the strong form he showed earlier in the season. With the ball, Taskin Ahmed and Shoriful Islam bring control with pace, while Rishad Hossain adds a spin option suited to these conditions. The pieces are there, it's about putting them together. New Zealand's system in motion - If the first game proved anything, it's that New Zealand's strength lies in their structure. Dean Foxcroft led the way with a composed 59 and chipped in with the ball, while Henry Nicholls once again showed his value with a steady hand at the top. Around them, the support continues to impress. Will Young adds solidity, while Tom Latham provides leadership and calmness in pressure situations. The bowling unit led by Blair Tickner and backed up by Nathan Smith, who combined for 7 wickets, showed how effective discipline and patience can be on these surfaces, with additional depth from players like Will O'Rourke. Even without their biggest names, this side continues to find ways to win, a reflection of their system and adaptability. Form and familiarity - Bangladesh still hold the advantage of familiarity with conditions and a core group that has enjoyed success at home, but New Zealand arrive with a winning habit, having dominated ODI series across opponents in the recent past. What the first game highlighted was how little separates the two sides, small moments, rather than big passages, could decide this contest again. Team form (Last 5 completed ODIs, recent first) - BAN - LWLWW | NZ - WWWLW. Conditions and the bigger picture - The Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium is expected to offer another slow, gripping surface where partnerships and game awareness will be key. With valuable points in the race for direct qualification to the 2027 ODI World Cup on the line, the stakes go beyond just this series, as Bangladesh are aiming to stay in contention, and New Zealand are looking to continue their momentum and close it out.
